# Text statistics (text.stats)

## categories

[
  "text"
]

## demonstrations

[
  {
    "expected_output": {
      "characters": 19,
      "lines": 2,
      "words": 3
    },
    "explanation": "The newline is a character; the last line has no trailing break but still counts.",
    "id": "two-lines",
    "input": {
      "text": "hello world\ngoodbye"
    },
    "title": "Two short lines"
  },
  {
    "expected_output": {
      "characters": 0,
      "lines": 0,
      "words": 0
    },
    "id": "empty",
    "input": {
      "text": ""
    },
    "title": "Empty text"
  },
  {
    "expected_output": {
      "characters": 6,
      "lines": 2,
      "words": 2
    },
    "explanation": "Each \r\n is two characters but one line break.",
    "id": "windows-line-endings",
    "input": {
      "text": "a\r\nb\r\n"
    },
    "title": "Windows line endings"
  }
]

## description

Returns exact counts for the supplied text. Words are maximal runs of non-whitespace characters. Lines are counted by line breaks (
, 
 or ), and a final line without a trailing break still counts. Use this instead of estimating lengths yourself.

[
  {
    "condition": "The 'text' argument is missing or is not a string.",
    "recovery": "Pass the text as a JSON string under the key 'text'.",
    "symptom": "The call is rejected before execution with an input validation error."
  }
]

## limitations

[
  "Characters are Unicode code points, not grapheme clusters, so some emoji count as more than one.",
  "Input longer than 1,000,000 characters is rejected."
]

      "type": "integer"
